summary.intent: Add direct keyboard shortcuts (P, s, x) to the memory loop TUI memories list view for quick lifecycle transitions (promote, suppress, archive) that bypass the wizard.
summary.outcome: Successfully added three new keyboard shortcuts to the memories tab that apply lifecycle transitions immediately with flash feedback messages, while preserving the wizard for more complex workflows.

repo: memorylooptui has a wizard path (enter/w) for complex lifecycle workflows like adopt-to-scope and apply-to-files, and a separate quick-action path for simple status transitions
Lifecycle actions are modeled as a LifecycleAction type with at least promote, suppress, and archive variants
Flash messages are used to confirm quick actions with format 'memory title → new_status'
The TUI is structured with a root model that delegates to tab models (tab_memories.go), with messages passed via quickLifecycleMsg

code.finding: Key bindings are defined here; P, s, x were added as new bindings for promote, suppress, archive
Message types for TUI events live here; quickLifecycleMsg was added to carry action+target to root
Key event handling in the memories tab emits quickLifecycleMsg on P/s/x keypresses
Root model handles quickLifecycleMsg via a new handleQuickLifecycle method added after handlePrune; hints/help text updated to show new shortcuts

workflow: Build and test were run after implementation to verify correctness before finalizing
The implementation followed a clear read-first pattern: all relevant files were read before any edits began

open_items: The wizard (enter/w) path for adopt-to-scope and apply-to-files workflows remains separate — no consolidation or cross-reference between quick actions and wizard flows was done
